Committee on Health and Human Services Re: LD 541 - An Act to Promote Awareness of the Maine Parentage Act
March 13, 2025
Senator Ingwersen, Representative Meyer, and distinguished members of the Committee on Health and Human Services, my name is Heide Lester, and I am a resident of Paris and the Deputy Director of EqualityMaine, which has been advocating on behalf of Maine's LGBTQ+ community since 1984. We strongly support building awareness of the Maine Parentage Act, a set of state laws that were passed in 2016 and strengthened in 2021.
The Maine Parentage Act clarifies the ways someone can legally establish that they are the parent of a child, and addresses who is able to establish legal parentage and how. It extends an accessible path to parentage for children born through assisted reproduction and for children born through surrogacy, and it secures greater protections and equal treatment for children of LGBTQ+ parents. In short, the Maine Parentage Act ensures that all children in the state have equal access to a secure parent-child relationship, which is essential for a child's health and well-being.
The law allows many LGBTQ+ parents in Maine to establish parentage through a simple form, ensuring parents are able to have their legal relationship to their child recognized immediately at birth or any time before the child turns 18. Yet many parents or those who hope to become parents are not aware that establishing parentage will allow them to make any early medical decisions in a child's life, ensure that a child will receive insurance benefits or inheritance rights, and protect parents' parental rights if they separate. Others believe that having their name on a child's birth certificate is sufficient. And some are confused or intimidated by the terminology and processes.
Over 20% of LGBTQ+ adults in Maine are raising children,1 and they can face challenges in building their families and keeping them safe. We are so fortunate to live in a state that recognizes the diversity of families and provides pathways to a legal parent-child relationship. We urge you to vote "Ought to Pass" on LD 541. Providing informational brochures about the Maine Parentage Act is a simple yet effective way to improve children's long-term well-being and stability.
Thank you,
Heide Lester (they/them) Deputy Director, EqualityMaine

Re: LD 541 - An Act to Promote Awareness of the Maine Parentage Act

Senator Ingwersen, Representative Meyer and members of the Joint Standing Committee on Health and Human Services, thank you for the opportunity to provide information in opposition to LD 541, An Act to Promote Awareness of the Maine Parentage Act.

This bill requires Maine CDC to develop and distribute an informational brochure that addresses basic questions about the Maine Parentage Act. This brochure is meant to be widely distributed to physician offices, hospitals and other public places. The estimated cost for printing brochures is $16,000, with additional costs for distribution.

Title 19-A chapter 61, Maine Parentage Act (Act), is comprehensive, covering various aspects of parentage1. Maine CDC appreciates the intent of this bill; however, there are existing systems to achieve the objective. Currently, information is available online on the Maine CDC Data, Research, and Vital Statistics (DRVS) office webpage, and this resource can be updated to include additional information. The acknowledgement or denial of parentage is administrative processes, though other sections of the Act, such as gestational carriers and de facto parentage, require adjudication, are outside of Maine CDC's scope of work, and may not be appropriate as part of the Department's online material. Additionally, information addressing frequently asked questions on the Act is being updated at this time to be posted on DRVS's website and be available for the public. (See attachment)

Widespread distribution of written material is not a cost-efficient way to disseminate information. Printed materials may become outdated leading to erroneous or conflicting information in print. There is also no way to assure that the information is getting to the intended target population. Maine municipalities and birthing hospitals have access to the Department's online brochures and DRVS forms and instructions and are notified when information is created or updated to ensure that outdated documentation is replaced. Updated information is publicly available for print and provided to individuals at their request.

1 The Maine Parentage Act establishes eight main mechanisms for establishing parentage - birth, adoption, acknowledgement, presumption, de facto parentage, genetic parentage, assisted reproduction, and gestational-carrier agreements. 19-A MRS � 1832(14) defines `parentage' to mean the legal relationship between a child and a parent as established in accordance with the Act.
Rev. 2/2025

Maine CDC opposes this legislation requiring the Department to distribute printed material specific to the Maine Parentage Act. Information available electronically that can be accessed and printed as needed and in response to individual requests is more practical, cost-effective and in line with other education and outreach efforts. LD 541 may not be necessary as the work described in the legislation is currently being undertaken; and DRVS is open to working with the Sponsor and the Committee to add the desired level of detail to this material for its public-facing website.
Please feel free to contact me if you have any questions during your deliberation of this bill.
Sincerely,
Puthiery Va Director Maine Center for Disease Control Maine Department of Health and Human Services
